subject: Performance gating, variant selection & MAP — Vertex Health POC
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance gating, variant selection & MAP — Vertex Health POC

Anna — great to meet yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a first-pass MAP and a focused performance benchmarking plan so we can align on go/no-go criteria for the POC. High level ask: agree the performance gates we will measure, which Redwood model variants to evaluate, and a close timeline so procurement can start paperwork.

Key pieces in the attached MAP (vertex_poc_map_v1.xlsx):
- Performance gates (technical): p95 latency at target concurrency, sustained throughput, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and model-quality pass thresholds.
- Variant matrix: candidate Redwood catalog variants (baseline, quantized, and smaller/faster variants) with estimated cost delta.
- Test harness: synthetic vs recorded traffic, 3 concurrency profiles (burst, sustained, peak), and evaluation metrics (semantic-similarity, response acceptability).
- Timeline: 3-week measurement window, final go/no-go on Tue 2026-08-04.

Proposed initial gates (draft — please comment):
- p95 token latency <= 220 ms at concurrency 60 (typical query shape for Vertex).
- Sustained throughput >= 1,200 tokens/s for 60 concurrent sessions (end-to-end, including prefix caching).
- TTFT <= 90 ms for cold sessions (first token time).
- Quality: semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.82 vs. baseline human references OR human accept rate >= 85% on a 200-sample set.

Candidate Redwood variants to benchmark (examples from our catalog):
- rw-c7-40b-fp16 (quality baseline)
- rw-c7-40b-q4 (quantized, lower-cost)
- rw-c7-13b-fp16 (faster, lower cost)
- rw-c7-13b-q4 (quantized smaller variant)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Anna to confirm stakeholders + sample traffic shape and whether we can run recorded traffic (helps TTFT measurement).
2) Jasmine to propose concrete test harness and measurement scripts + expected artifacts.
3) Karthik to confirm commercial gating and timeline.

I've attached benchmarks_20260715.csv with initial synthetic run numbers (very preliminary) and sample_traffic_telemetry.json for your team to review. If this plan looks good we'll lock the MAP and schedule an engineering kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Performance gating, variant selection & MAP — Vertex Health POC

Anna / Priyom — quick technical plan from the SE side. I built a reproducible harness that we can run against recorded or synthetic traffic (attached both). Implementation notes:

- Measurement harness: k6 load driver + Redwood SDK wrapper. Measures per-request TTFT, per-token emission rate, and end-to-end latency including network. We produce raw traces + aggregated histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99).
- Concurrency profiles:
  * Sustained: 60 concurrent sessions @ steady arrival rate (matches prod median)
  * Burst: 120 concurrent sessions for 30s windows (simulates traffic spikes)
  * Cold-start: single-session cold runs to measure TTFT and kernel warmups
- Dataset for quality: 200 anonymized prompts (you mentioned you'll share) + 50 hard-edge prompts for targeted failure modes. Automated metrics: embedding cosine similarity, ROUGE-L for structured outputs, and human accept panel on 200 samples.
- Variant comparisons: we'll run the same suite on the four variants Priyom listed. For each variant we will record: p95 latency, tokens/sec, TTFT, memory utilization, and a simple quality score (composite of embedding cosine and human accept rate).

Preliminary expectations (from small-scale lab runs):
- rw-c7-40b-fp16: highest quality (baseline), p95 ~ 300 ms at concurrency 60 (no prefix cache), tokens/sec ~ 900.
- rw-c7-40b-q4: quality ~ -2 to -4 points on our composite quality score vs baseline, p95 improvement ~ 25–30%.
- rw-c7-13b-fp16: quality ~ -6 to -10 points vs baseline, p95 ~ 170–220 ms, tokens/sec ~ 1,400–1,800.
- rw-c7-13b-q4: best cost profile, quality drop concentrated on long-form summarization tasks.

Artifacts we will produce: per-variant CSV with latency histograms, cost-per-token estimate (USD), and a short narrative with edge-case failure examples. I'll include a reproducible script and a Dockerfile so Vertex can run the same harness in VPC if needed.

Let me know if you can provide the sample set (anonymized) by EOD 2026-07-17 so we can queue the runs the week of 07/20.

-- Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Team — short commercial note to align expectations and close timeline. Priyom, please add this language to the MAP and SOW:

- POC length: 3 weeks of active benchmarking + 1 week for results review. Target decision date: 2026-08-05.
- Acceptance: pass/fail per gate with signed acceptance form. If Redwood misses agreed-upon p95 or TTFT SLOs for more than two of the primary gates, Vertex will be eligible for a one-time credit (negotiable, add to SOW).
- Deployment option: Vertex has requested VPC run during the POC; Redwood will provide Private deployment access for testing (limited-time credentials + audit logging). Add a short security appendix referencing our SOC2 report.
- Commercial: if POC passes, we will issue an MSA + reserved capacity proposal within 10 business days.

Action items and owners: 
- Priyom: finalize MAP + DocuSign SOW by 2026-07-17 (attachment: vertex_poc_map_v1.xlsx).
- Jasmine: run the benchmark suite and share per-variant CSVs by 2026-07-31 (attachments: benchmarks_20260715.csv, sample_traffic_telemetry.json).
- Maria/Vertex: deliver anonymized 200-sample set by 2026-07-17.
- Karthik: prepare credit language and draft reserved capacity proposal pending pass.

If everyone agrees to the dates above I will prepare the DocuSign SOW and commercial appendix.

Thanks — Karthik
